svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Nitrogen (from the air) and hydrogen (from natural gas) are mixed in a 1 : 3 ratio."], [2, "The compressor raises the pressure to about 200 atm."], [4, "In the reactor the gases pass over an iron catalyst at about 450 \u00b0C: N\u2082 + 3H\u2082 \u21cc 2NH\u2083. Only about 15% reacts."], [7.5, "In the condenser the mixture is cooled: ammonia condenses to a liquid and is removed."], [10, "The unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are recycled back through the reactor, so very little is wasted."], [13, "Conditions are a compromise: high pressure gives a good yield and rate; 450 \u00b0C gives a fast enough rate; the catalyst speeds it up but does not change the yield."]]
svg.title: The Haber process
svg.desc: Flow diagram: nitrogen and hydrogen are compressed to 200 atm, react over an iron catalyst at 450 °C, ammonia is condensed and removed, and unreacted gases are recycled.

g.data-info: Air is about 78% nitrogen. It is separated by fractional distillation of liquid air.
Methane reacts with steam: CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂ (then CO + H₂O → CO₂ + H₂).
Compresses the 1 : 3 mixture of N₂ and H₂ to about 200 atm. Higher pressure shifts the equilibrium to the right (4 gas molecules → 2) and speeds up the reaction.
Gases pass over beds of iron catalyst at about 450 °C. Only about 15% of the mixture becomes ammonia per pass.
Speeds up the reaction so equilibrium is reached faster. It does not change the position of equilibrium (the yield).
The mixture is cooled. Ammonia has a much higher boiling point than N₂ and H₂, so it condenses to a liquid.
Removed and stored; used mainly to make fertilisers (e.g. ammonium nitrate), and nitric acid.
Unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are pumped back to the reactor, so overall about 98% is converted.
N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH = −92 kJ mol⁻¹. 450 °C, 200 atm, iron catalyst: a compromise between yield, rate and cost.
g.text: High pressure: equilibrium shifts right (4 gas molecules → 2) and the rate rises, but high pressure is expensive and dangerous.
Forward reaction is exothermic: a low temperature gives a higher yield but is too slow, so 450 °C is a compromise. The iron catalyst speeds it up; the yield is unchanged.
